The sixteenth project report: F39's control is a result, and what stands between it and the goal

2026-10-07HEAD 1b14e55branch praneetdhoolia/sixteenth-report-and-gold-standard (one commit behind HEAD of main: 1b14e559 is main's tip; the branch holds the in-flight .gitignore edit only)gate PASS

F39's control arm is a result - 250 of 250 iterations in 27.85 h, the first 25 % arm since F37 to finish in one JVM and the first launched under the restart guard - and it reads 2 of 12 modes inside 10 % (car +8.5 %, motorbike -4.1 %), up from 1 of 12 on F38 because the fifteenth report's recommendation to scale motorcycle availability by the SMVU daily-use ratio did what it predicted. Eight modes stay past the 20 % stop bar, and every one of them is now traced to a measured mechanism rather than a constant: walk loses the short trips to a car that pays no terminal time (59.2 % of sub-kilometre trips driven) and wins the long trips of the car-less who have no driver and no transit route (47.6 % of pt requests unserved); rail is reached by the car-less on long walks; the pt submode split has no frequency term. The code closes 12 of the fifteenth report's 21 findings; the four defects at HEAD are in the instruments, not the model (the watcher's cutoff ignores a resume's first iteration, the hardcoding gate runs for one city while Mumbai's ledger reads 233, a shrink-only ceiling admits any logged rise, and the manifest names the wrong producer for the one observation D28 rests on). The documents moved from 2 to 3 and stop there on one pattern - a fact typed by hand beside a generated one: the lane's family stamp, closed issues cited by open work, two pages still stamped for F35. The lane's recommended arm answers an issue closed on 13 September, so the issue gate cannot see the treatment's measurement. In the field this repository is still the only project on the per-mode ridership rung, and the field has now published both the case this project is in - survey shares right, counts wrong, fixed by background traffic from the count residuals - and in-run calibration at a tenth of this project's cost per evaluation. The factor ledger ranks the car terminal time (OUT) first and the built-and-unrun headway charge (INERT) second. The next act is the F39 pair under D29; then one family for the terminal time and the car-less alternative; and, before either, the instrument fixes this report names, every one of which needs no run.

Method

One pass at HEAD 1b14e559 (main's tip, 30 September 2026), read on 7 October 2026 after the gate passed. The mechanical half came from the three collectors (collect_metrics.py: 4,005 files on disk, 709 commits, 94 pull requests, 165 issues, 200 CI runs, 250 run-index rows, 393 dated events over 58 days; collect_code_metrics.py: 419 Python files / 96,743 lines and 86 Java files / 22,324 lines, thresholds long function 150 lines, complex 15 branches, nesting 5, duplicate window 6 lines; collect_performance.py: 249 runs, 51 with a stopwatch). Six agents then ran in parallel, one per phase, none twice: a code reviewer over the six areas starting from code_metrics.json's ranked rows with a declared depth of read per area; a performance analyst over performance.json, the runs' own stopwatch and gc logs and the Java listeners; a historian over every pull request body, the commit log, the timeline and the fifteen earlier reports with the recommendation ledger; a document, process, controls and issues reviewer over every living and archived document, every hook, workflow and skill, the last five sessions' records and pull requests, and the issue set; a field researcher and a factor researcher, each starting from the reference library and spending at most 40 searches on its gaps. The twelve-mode table was built by the writer from the board's reader re-run on the control (report_mode_ridership.py --run 20260929T072135_250it_25pct --it 250), the run's _fit.json, the target table and the position pages. Ratings use the rubric 5 exemplary with evidence, 4 sound with minor issues, 3 works with real gaps, 2 defects likely, 1 broken; every cell carries its two strongest pieces of evidence and, where below 4, the smallest change that would honestly justify a 4, because this pass precedes a session whose directive is every cell at 4 or better. Nothing in this report is a result unless the run it cites carries ran_to_last_iteration; nothing was edited under src/, cities/ or the living documents, and no run was launched or recompiled.

The timeline from day 0

  • 10 Aug: the package, the network and the tour demand land in three PRs on day 0; P4 opens on 11 Aug when MATSim refuses the inputs (#4).
  • 11-16 Aug: the registry (297 fields, zero hardcoding) and the issue-32 network rebuild in one 73-commit PR (#38); the first 1000-iteration arms run on 16-17 Aug.
  • 18-21 Aug: ride pairing, escort binding and the all-physical model (#40-#58) in a stacked week; the direct-commit ban (#61) and F4's two 1000-iteration arms on 21 Aug.
  • 24-25 Aug: C5 exists; the SUMO descope and the all-modes batch (#79-#81) cross the F6 activation boundary; the documents pinned to artefacts (#83, #85).
  • 26-30 Aug: the gate loop under the /goal directive: F7-F21 open in five days, eight families on 30 Aug alone, with 31 record sections and 87 commits that day; four self-corrections recorded (#95).
  • 30 Aug - 3 Sep: GOAL.md, the one-page board and the position pages (#101); the first gate since F4 (F21, #104); fares (#105); the results store (#106); the 25 % directive (1 Sep); requirement 10 and the issue gate (#111).
  • 3-8 Sep: the report series starts (#138); five reports in five days drive 29-of-34 defect closures, the holdout leak, the iteration profile (310 -> 205 s) and the objective restated on twelve modes (#166).
  • 9-14 Sep: the first result since F4 (F32, 0 of 12, #173); the choice-set ceiling for ride (#176); F33's arm dies on an unset heap (#179); the footpath rebuild (#194); F35 arm 0 lands 2 of 12 (#201); the documents move to docs/ and split (#218, #219).
  • 15-18 Sep: two F35 pairs (routers, scoring) are nulls (#226, #233); Codex skills (#236); the 19 Sep Mumbai sessions (9.179-9.200) run without PRs.
  • 21-23 Sep: Mumbai lands on the framework in eight PRs (#240-#251); the roots rebuild opens F36 (#254); F36 arm 0 is killed by a Windows Update restart at it.237.
  • 25-30 Sep: report #14's three defects fixed (#256, F37); F37, F38 (three warm starts across a session kill, an NVMe crash and a shutdown) and F39's control all reach 250: 2, 1, 2 of 12; the headway charge is found keyed on route variants and rebuilt (#259).
  • 30 Sep - 7 Oct: no commit, no session, no run; the F39 treatment arm waits on D29 - the longest quiet stretch of the project (8.8 days against a previous maximum merge gap of 4.76 days).

architecture
The framework builders under src/build/ read every value from the registry and write city-relative artefacts the manifest hashes; the two city build directories are adapters. Since the fifteenth report the plans writer gained a third seeded stream (motorbike_daily_use) that thins possession to daily use at the SMVU ratio, refuses a choice build whose observed availability tables are absent (require_motorbike_tables, build_matsim_plans.py:343-361), and the run-input assembler emits the ATAP M1 price. Builders now record their own wall time through build_timing.py, which closes the fourteenth and fifteenth reports' 'no build timing' finding at the two builders that call it. The Mumbai chain is seven scripts whose main() functions are 155-215 lines each; they share no stage helpers with the Newcastle adapters and keep a parallel run-input assembler (build_baseline_run_inputs.py, 317 lines).

architecture
Launch resolves the registry through overlays, preflights every refusal before the subsample, then either detaches under the Task Scheduler (Windows) or runs here. Since fe419200 an arm-length foreground run must prove it was started by its own live scheduled task (stamp + per-launch nonce in the environment, task RUNNING and carrying the nonce), a resume's innovation cutoff is recomputed with the jar's own int truncation and refused on a mismatch against the parent's _config.json snapshot, a pid the kernel will not describe is UNKNOWN and --stop records died only when the run's log confirms silence longer than its longest iteration, and every progress write carries the host's CPU, RAM and top other process. The stop test states its processes live (fc38ccd9) instead of reading the host's process table. The harness is Windows-first by decision D6; on POSIX the new proof cannot be supplied and --detach is refused, so no arm can launch there at all.

architecture
Every reader resolves a run through results_store, reads the run's own _config.json for its resolution and its _run.json for what is citable, and the board renders only what the record allows (build_status_board.py:189-192). Since the fifteenth report the fit is mirrored into processed/ at write time so a trim cannot delete the only copy (fit.py:674-678), two demographic readers take a bare run name like every other (results_store.resolve), the pricer prices a resume from its checkpoint, and the digest carries the host's load. The viewer (run_view.py) and the twelve-mode reader are each ~1,490 lines and each carry their own readable_iterations; the reached_iteration clamp lives in the board and the point reader, not in iteration_reading where every reader would inherit it.

architecture
The portable half (config/schema/) is generated from the reference city's registry by render_schema and checked against every city by check_city; the emitted MATSim config is proven to move with every bound field by check_hardcoding question 7; the living documents are pinned to artefacts by check_doc_currency/check_doc_shape; the manifest hashes every data file. Since the fifteenth report the manifest check runs for every city in the gate and CI with the debt moved out of the framework into cities/<city>/tests/manifest_debt.json under a ceiling that needs a dated log entry to rise, provenance records are dated by rule and verified inside, the config reference is checked for every city, the gate carries every script CI runs (test_gate_covers_ci), and a NUL-byte check guards tracked sources after ServiceQualityScoring.java shipped with two of them. One asymmetry remains: check_hardcoding, the ledger CLAUDE.md says 'is at 0 and stays at 0', is run for the default city only and reports 233 items for Mumbai.

architecture
Every acquisition lands under data/raw/ with a provenance record and is immutable; the extract layer turns it into processed tables that the manifest hashes with a lineage scope and licence. Mumbai's 578 provenance records are harvests (zip archives with a members listing and fixed entry timestamps) and a data-use ledger says what each source feeds. Since the fifteenth report the raw-row date rule exempts provenance records by rule and verifies the date inside them (check_manifest.py:324-348), which took Mumbai's undated raw debt from 579 rows to 1 and Newcastle's from 15 to 2. The harbour-line evidence chain is seven scripts that hash their inputs before and after, refuse any disagreement, and export nothing as a schedule; their complexity is the evidence's, not an accident.

architecture
CitysimControler assembles the stock Controler with the citysim config groups, listeners and QSim components in a fixed order; every mechanism is gated by a registry field whose OFF value recovers the previous family byte for byte, and each D28 mechanism ships with a probe proving both halves. The engines keep per-iteration state written by the handler threads and read at the sim-step barrier (RunTelemetry and RidePairingEngine refuse to exist without it); the signals stack lives in a second class tree that shares the base assembly. Since the fifteenth report: trip ends are bounded by link capacity at startup (ActivityLinkCapacity), a household's riders share one motorcycle through the same roster and departure handler as the household car, a no-route pt walk beyond the declared reach is stamped and scored as an unexecutable plan rather than refused (MATSim's null-route answer would teleport a beeline), and the headway charge reads the boarded line's departures at the boarding stop (one key per parent stop, pt2matsim's child suffix stripped) with ATAP M1 as a declared alternative function.

Eight probes are listed in run_signal_probes.py and run in the gate when the toolchain is idle: SignalsAssemblyProbe, TramPriorityProbe, GatedSubtourProbe, NestedSubtourProbe, ActivityRetimesProbe, EscortCoherenceProbe, PtNoRouteWalkProbe, ActivityLinkCapacityProbe, HouseholdMotorcycleProbe, ServiceQualityProbe (the last four new since 6bc18487; HouseholdMotorcycleProbe runs the real assemble() on a temp toy). None runs in CI (test.yml has no Java step). TaxiFleetEngine has no allocation probe; EscortCoherenceProbe has no repeated-link plan. Thread safety rests on the barrier two classes enforce and the signals classes assume.

how_phase_shares_moved_between_families
F35 scoring pair (16 Sep) -> F37 (26 Sep) -> F39 control (29 Sep), plain innovating iteration: 356 -> 358 -> 345 s. Replanning 93 -> 104 -> 78 s (-25 % F37 -> F39: RUN.transit_router.no_route_walk = refused_beyond_reach refused 358,146 no-route walks beyond 3,224 m over the arm, so the pt router splices fewer long network walks); mobsim 246 -> 227 -> 237 s (+4.4 % F37 -> F39 with departures 2,803,427 -> 2,952,577, +5.3 %: the mobsim is linear in departures); beforeMobsim 23 -> 21 -> 17 s. Tail plain 265 -> 272.5 -> 274.5 s. Shares of the control: mobsim 66.4 % (F37 59.3 %, F35 67.4 %), replanning 19.7 % (26.7 %, 22.3 %). Wall 25.77 -> 31.43 -> 27.85 h; the difference between arms is the host stretch (F37 5.56 h, F39 2.09 h, F35 none), not the build. At 1 % (20260929T055640_2it_1pct, F39 smoke, 8 threads, 18g): 53.8 s per iteration, mobsim 36 s, 116,723 departures, 2,473 departures per wall second - 25.3x the departures cost 6.4x the wall; the sampling position page states no pace-scaling law, the runs page's pace band [217, 253] is the 25 % x 1000 band it calls meaningless until re-measured, and no run longer than 2 iterations exists at 1 % on the current build, so the scaling is unmeasured on this build.

binding

Verdict on the 250-iteration horizon

The 250-iteration horizon is reachable at the measured pace and was reached in 27.85 h by F39's control (20260929T072135_250it_25pct) against a 27.7 h quote - the first arm since F37 to finish in one JVM and the first launched under the restart guard - with a plain innovating iteration of 345 s, a tail of 260-275 s, and the mobsim at 237 s (66 %) and replanning at 78 s (20 %, down a quarter on F37 with the bounded no-route walk). On an idle host the same arm is ~25.8 h: 2.09 h of it was a band at iterations 160-205 in which every phase slowed together and the collector paused 0.81 h in 21 full collections over 60 s, the paging signature of F37's 5.56 h stretch, and nothing recorded what else the host was doing. Halving the arm (~14 h) is not reachable by result-preserving levers: a host guard and history (0-2 h), one events pass (minutes), build-time routing (0.33 h), a refused-taxi route cache (0.36 h) and a smaller heap (unmeasured) sum to at most ~3 h; the 18.2 h mobsim at 8,451 departures per wall second on 16 of 24 cores has not been profiled since 12 September, so what would halve it - walk off the qsim (reverses F34, opens a family), fewer innovating iterations (touches results), or a parallel-efficiency fix the profile has to find - is unmeasured and needs a probe arm.

what the comparison says

  • Across 61 projects the top rung (per-mode ridership, every simulated mode) is still empty; this repository is the only row attempting it, and it reads 2 of 12 inside 10 % (car +8.5 %, motorbike -4.1 %) on F39's control at 250 of 250 iterations.
  • The field's answer to 'shares right, counts wrong' is now in print with numbers (Samaei et al., Paris, MUM 2026): the missing vehicles are non-resident demand - freight, services, visitors - solved from the detector residuals as background agents (hourly count R2 0.669 -> 0.887), never a behavioural constant. This project's count deficit sits in the same family and its trucks are count shares.
  • Two agency activity-based models publish boardings by transit type with deviations, and both miss where this project misses: PSRC 2015 ferry -81.9 % (AM) and light rail -39.9 % (midday) with the total inside 2 %; MWCOG 2025 commuter rail VRE at 0.81 with the total at 1.01. A per-mode miss on the small transit modes is the field's norm, not this twin's peculiarity.
  • Calibration cost is being attacked inside the run: Dib & Balac calibrate 26 canton constants in one 90-iteration MATSim run at 8-13 % overhead, and Sallard & Balac calibrate raptor sub-mode weights and transfer-type penalties with no mobsim at all - against this project's one 27.9 h arm per evaluation.
  • Motorcycle-majority agent-based models exist on two rungs now - Jakarta (MRT smartcard, +8.16 %) and Meerut (counts, 49 % of links within GEH < 10) - and both raise the seepage question (smaller vehicles passing queued larger ones) this project's motorbike at pce 0.4 does not ask; the Jakarta row traces three-quarters of new rail riders to motorcycles.
  • Physical fidelity measured against an observation now has a stored case (Munich-Schwabing, TUM): microscopic SUMO on MATSim demand agrees 'considerably better' with real speeds than the mesoscopic model - on speeds, not counts; no row yet measures signals, dwell or parking against a count or boarding figure.
  • What a warm start buys is measured for the first time (Zame et al.): reconvergence after a perturbation took 26-208 iterations for one and the same iteration-0 deficit, governed by the new configuration's quality rather than the size of the change - the treatments most likely to improve a scenario cost most to re-converge.
  • A calibrated base is not a scenario base (Tel Aviv, Replan): the line-level count correction that fits the base year is removed before forecasting because it would 'prevent the passenger redistribution that MATSim is supposed to simulate'; R2 0.976 on line volumes survives the release, the exact line fit does not.

data acquired answer

Unchanged in kind this pass: car on 30 RMS permanent count stations plus holdout; heavy and light rail on Opal station entries and stop-level trips; bus on Opal trips by contract region (not the per-service BOAM occupancy); ferry on disclosed tap-on bounds with the Stockton CSV still a data-lane download (gap 20); taxi and ride as derived bands; bike and walk on HTS shares with no counter layer; motorbike on BITRE stock and ABS SMVU daily use; trucks on classified heavy-vehicle shares; signals on TfNSW locations with SCATS as its algorithm. Against the field: AToM holds 48 + 48 active-mode counters this twin lacks; Jakarta and Cape Town hold smartcard OD this twin holds only as aggregates; Paris (Samaei) holds 1,892 detectors and TomTom route times; Meerut holds crowdsourced link travel times. The one acquisition the field's new rows make urgent is a through-and-freight residual on the counted links (Samaei's background traffic), derivable from data already in the manifest.

physical fidelity answer

This twin runs every mode in the mobsim: four transit modes on the mapped GTFS with SCATS and TSP on 14 corridor systems, level crossings from the timetable, walk and bike on a 40,203-way footpath network with pt access/egress/transfer walks executed as network legs (teleported = 0), priced parking with search time, Opal fares, income-scaled money, motorbike chosen by daily use at pce 0.4. The field has not yet shown fidelity moving a VALIDATION figure: the one new stored case (Munich-Schwabing) measures micro vs meso on speeds; Dresden calibrates bridge capacities to counts (a capacity, not a fidelity, change); Char Dham's per-link FIFO/PassingQ is validated on corridor travel times (R2 0.96-0.99) but never compared with uniform dynamics. This project's own one-field pairs (the routers pair: a null; F39's four corrections: motorbike -4.1 % from +466 %, across a family boundary) remain the only readings of representation changes against the twelve-mode scoreboard.

validation_rung
per-mode ridership, every simulated mode - the top rung, and still the only project in this survey of 55 attempting it for twelve modes. The pass of 9 September qualified the claim (a four-step model, WFTDM, does report six transit modes inside 10%); THIS pass qualifies it further and more precisely: the WFRC ActivitySim framework's own Table 29 lists 'Transit boardings by transit mode' as a standard validation summary, so per-transit-mode granularity is normal agency practice for an activity-based model. What no other row does is treat every one of twelve modes as a SCORED TARGET WITH A BAND that the calibration is obliged to satisfy simultaneously. | 2026-09-16: unchanged - still the only row in 55 that scores every simulated mode as a target with a band; BEAM CORE, read this pass, names three observation families (speeds/VMT, MTC shares, agency boardings) and publishes no level fit for any. | 2026-09-29 (fifteenth pass): unchanged - still the only row in 58 scoring every simulated mode as a target with a band; the reading on it fell from 2 to 1 of 12 inside 10 % (F38's arm 0). The field's nearest agency analogues (PSRC per operator, MWCOG and CMAP per transit mode) validate transit by operator or submode, not every mode at once. | 2026-10-07 (sixteenth pass): unchanged in kind - still the only row in 61 scoring every simulated mode as a target with a band; the reading is back to 2 of 12 inside 10 % on F39's control. The field now holds TWO agency rows with per-transit-type deviation tables (MWCOG 2025; PSRC 2015, read this pass, which names a ferry miss of -81.9 % AM and a light-rail miss of -39.9 % midday - the two families this project misses most), and a NEW ROW (Jakarta MRT) on the transit-ridership rung for a single mode.

status
active, in calibration - P4 at HEAD 1b14e559 (sixty-fourth session, 30 September 2026; read 7 October 2026). Registry 600 fields, manifest 968 files, 30 assembled run-input sets (board state block). F39 is open with its CONTROL a result (2 of 12); its headway treatment is rebuilt on the line at its stop with ATAP M1's valuation and unrun (D29; probes quoted 27.7-50.5 h). The newest run on disk 20260930T140500_4it_25pct ran to its last iteration as a pricing probe. Heap rule 37.4 GiB at 25 % against a measured live peak of 30.0 GiB.
does_best
Every controllable value declared with units, provenance and a sweep or held-fixed rule (558 fields), every living number pinned to its artefact by a check, twelve modes each monitored on its own basis every tenth iteration - and, unique in this survey, a REGISTRY-ENFORCED refusal to fit a constant over a named missing mechanism (C.asc.rail's departure_requires clause). THIS PASS ADDS A SECOND UNIQUENESS, AND IT IS THE HONEST ONE: the project's _fit.json scores mode shares, absolute link counts, trip-length geometry and vehicle occupancy IN ONE ARTEFACT FROM ONE RUN, names its 32 unscorable targets with reasons, and refuses to call a stopped arm a result. Across 53 surveyed projects, the closest published analogues each hold part of that - AToM validates five observation families but calibrates against one; Tallinn optimises three target families at once but reports no per-mode transit rung; the WFRC framework enumerates every validation summary but states outright that not all of them can be met simultaneously. | 2026-09-14: against the three rows added this pass the position sharpens - Cape Town reaches the tap-data rung for ONE operator with ~25 hand-tuned runs; mobiTopp Stuttgart calibrates trip-length distributions and modal split jointly but by eye; Barcelona runs generic actuated signals at 2,035 intersections on full demand for R2 0.81 on counts and nothing else. None scores more than one observation family with a stated band. | 2026-09-14 (tenth pass): the claim is now made against a RESULT with 2 of 12 inside 10 % rather than 0 - and against 55 rows. The two rows added this pass sharpen it from opposite sides: Barcelona-MATSim (2019) validates on counts it never calibrated on and names the excluded demand behind its two misses, which this project's fit module does for its 32 unscorable targets but not yet for its count outliers; Rotterdam-The Hague (2025) removes mode choice from MATSim altogether so that one calibrator owns it, where this project's twelve constants are scored inside the co-evolutionary loop they must survive. | 2026-09-16 (twelfth pass): the claim is now made against a THIRD result and the first one-field pair reading in the survey - a null. The BEAM update this pass sharpens the comparison from the sample side: BEAM calibrates at 10 %, validates at 30 % and states that an on-demand mode needs 40 % before its dynamics settle; this project reads taxi and ride at 25 % and scores them with a band, which no BEAM paper does. | 2026-09-29 (fifteenth pass): unchanged against 58 rows. The MUM 2026 programme shows the MATSim community moving toward automated multi-source calibration (seven talks), where this project's contraction test and _fit.json already sit; none of those talks yet publishes a per-mode band. | 2026-10-07 (sixteenth pass): against 61 rows. Three things read this pass bracket this project from new sides: Samaei et al. (Paris) publish exactly this project's count deficit and fix it with non-resident background demand rather than a constant - the same refusal this project's registry encodes for C.asc.rail; Dib & Balac fold the share calibration INTO the run at 8-13 % overhead, where this project pays one 28 h arm per evaluation; and PSRC's 2015 table shows an agency ABM missing ferry by -82 % and light rail by -40 % at midday while its total boardings sit within 2 % - the same two modes this project misses most, which says the miss is a known family, not a peculiarity of this twin.

calibration_method
family
coordinate descent over registry-declared sweeps (unchanged, never run to completion) PLUS, NEW AT THIS HEAD AND NEVER RUN, an implemented ASC log-ratio fixed point - src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py. Read from the source at HEAD 781cf41, not searched.
what_the_source_says
src/calibrate/calibrate.py:508-533 runs coordinate descent: per round, per free parameter, per grid point across that parameter's registry sweep, a FULL MATSim run -> extract_metrics -> fit -> a weighted scalar objective over declared _fit.json components, keeping a point only if it is feasible against the C4 occupancy and trip-length constraints; the round stops when the improvement falls below delta. The search space is DERIVED FROM THE REGISTRY, not listed in the script: a field is free only if it is source=assumed, carries a scalar sweep and is not held_fixed. The six mode constants are held_fixed under DECISIONS.md 8.5 and are therefore unreachable from the loop by construction - so this project has NO log(target/modelled) ASC loop of any kind. The one constant that is solved, asc_car_passenger, is solved in a separate module (solve_asc_ride.py:101-121) by SECANT INTERPOLATION ON log(ride_per_car) against the observed passenger:driver ratio, and is reported as a CONSTRAINT, not an estimate. The loop refuses to fit more parameters than the objective identifies (four independent numbers) and cannot read a holdout row by construction.
objective_evaluations
coordinate descent: calibrate.py:433 computes the budget as sum(len(grid(p, points_per_param)) for p in free) * max_rounds FULL MATSim runs; at 25% an arm reaching iteration 100 cost 7.66 h wall, so a 3-point 3-parameter 2-round search is ~18 arms and ~140 machine hours. THE LOOP HAS NEVER BEEN RUN TO COMPLETION. The ASC fixed point is far cheaper by design - TWO arms settle the contraction question - and is the only one of the two that has an evaluation count small enough to state in advance. Neither has been executed.
convergence_criterion
round-over-round objective improvement < delta

asc_fixed_point_new_this_pass
src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py EXISTS and PROPOSES ONLY; it has NEVER BEEN RUN. It applies delta_i = damping * [ ln(target_i/modelled_i) - ln(target_ref/modelled_ref) ] against car as reference - the same object as the Berry (1994) share inversion and the same expression matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools computes verbatim, with the damping declared on CAL.asc.damping. THREE DESIGN CHOICES ARE UNUSUAL AND WORTH RECORDING: (1) THE TEST IS THE CONTRACTION, NOT THE SHARES - two damped rounds are compared mode by mode, and if |delta| shrinks the residual is a taste that constants will close, while if it does not shrink the deficit is STRUCTURAL and no constant will ever close it. That is a cheap, decisive, published-in-spirit answer to the 'constant or mechanism' question that the agency protocol answers only by ordering. (2) It CANNOT REACH A FROZEN CONSTANT: it reads held_fixed from the registry and refuses, structurally, the way the holdout guard refuses. (3) On heavy rail and light rail the step is marked basis_is_boardings and reported as a PROXY, because the logit inversion is exact only for shares of a common total. ROUND 1 IS PROPOSED OFF THE F31 GATE AND NOT APPLIED: bike -0.5121, bus -0.2301, ferry +0.6713, light rail +0.4143.
read_against_the_field_this_pass
Two published methods now bracket this project's loop and both were read this pass. (1) Chen, Prakash, Lima de Azevedo & Ben-Akiva (2020, TR-C 119:102650) names this project's coordinate descent for what it is: 'myopic heuristics in the sense that they do not consider the fundamental inter-dependencies among choice-models and do not have a systematic way to adjust model parameters' - and their non-myopic alternative calibrates precisely this project's target set at once (activity shares, mode shares, mode-specific OD flows, mode-specific sensor counts). (2) The WFRC/RSG ActivitySim framework publishes New ASC = Old ASC + ln(Target Proportion / Model Proportion) verbatim - the exact expression in asc_fixed_point.py - inside a CYCLIC protocol over model components, and states plainly that 'It is typically the case that not all calibration and validation targets can be achieved simultaneously.' | 2026-09-11 (third bracket): POLARIS's published procedure is the same cyclic ASC-by-purpose update, TIERED by iteration so that 'network state' can 'adapt to this change in demand' before the next tier is touched, with counts and speeds explicitly outside the calibrated set ('can only be minimally calibrated'). MATSim-NYC calibrated NO demand constants at all - its nested logit was estimated on RHTS + TLC/FHV/Citi Bike records and converted analytically - and spent its six SPSA iterations on twelve link-CAPACITY factors instead, which is the opposite allocation to this project's.

warm_start
--warm-start <dead run dir> exists in src/run/run_matsim.py: it resumes from a dead run's newest plans checkpoint, records warm_started_from, and RE-DERIVES RUN.replanning.fraction_to_disable_innovation so the innovation cutoff ITERATION is the parent's (the pinned jar's first + f x (last - first) had moved it 240 -> 260 at N = 100, #192). It is crash recovery, not a bit-identical continuation. Arm 0 of F35 dumps plans every 25 iterations for exactly this reason (the F33 arm that died at 98 had checkpoints at it.0 and it.1 only). This matches the platform's own answer (MATSim issue #834: restart AT the checkpoint iteration from its post-replanning plans); the platform has no finer mechanism, and the interval is the whole trade. No surveyed row states a warm start from a prior calibrated run except as the matsim-scenarios practice of shipping calibrated output plans as input plans. | 2026-09-14: arm 0 ran with warm_started_from: null and dumped plans every 25 iterations (12 checkpoints, 522-898 s each, ~50 min of the arm); it did not need the mechanism. Across the field this pass, Kelheim v3.0's published output is a single 388-iteration run and Rotterdam-The Hague's outer loop restarts MATSim per LOS iteration; no surveyed row checkpoints or warm-starts a calibration arm. | 2026-10-07: F39's control ran cold (no warm start) to 250 in 27.85 h; F38's arm 0 was joined at 75, 175 and 225. Zame et al. (MUM 2026, excluded, recorded) now give the field's first measurement of reconvergence after a perturbation: 26-208 iterations for one deficit, governed by the perturbed layout's quality not the move's size - a warning that the treatments most likely to improve a scenario cost most to re-converge.

That bears directly on this project's 25 % directive and its taxi (+142.6 %) and ride modes: an on-demand mode simulated at 25 % is on the steep part of BEAM's curve.

Barcelona traffic digital twin (SUMO; Getting Real, ISPRS IJGI 11(1) 24)SUMO agent-based microsimulation with duaIterate; two dynamic-assignment schemes compared on the same demand: In-Simulation Adaptive Rerouting (iSAR, with c-Logit and Gawron route-choice updates) and an iterative DUE (IIDUE). Author: Javier Argota Sanchez-Vaquerizo, Computational Social Science, ETH Zurich.Metropolitan Region of Barcelona (RMB) as the extended demand area: 3,126 km2, 5,151,263 people (2019), 17,430,628 trips of any mode; the simulation core 'Rondes' (inside the ring roads): 182.55 km2, 2,411,755 people. Network (Table 2): RMB 204,935 links, 98,752 intersections, 3,567 traffic lights, 577 TAZ; Rondes 25,307 links, 13,993 intersections, 2,035 traffic lights, 296 TAZ, 10,496 virtual induction loops.road link counts - the 488 permanent counting stations of the city of Barcelona, aggregated to AADT because 'only Monthly Average Daily Traffic (MADT) counts are publicly available'; plus the hourly demand profile against the survey curve (DTW distance) and the teleport rate as a sanity check. No transit, no active-mode, no mode-share validation (car only).Linear regression of simulated against observed AADT at the 488 detectors, averaged over the iSAR runs: 'a slope of 0.91 and an R2 value of 0.81 ... which can be considered a good match'; the paper's own bar is 'R2 > 0.8 is considered a good fit'; NRMSE ~0.385 at device.rerouting.probability = 1 and weights.priority-factor = 100; ~5 % of vehicles teleported; 'the results from the IIDUE method reach worse values for both metrics'. The share of monitored links with GEH < 5 is plotted (Figure 5h) but not stated as a number in the text. The simulated hourly demand sits 'slightly lower ... particularly in peak hours' because congestion delays vehicle insertion. Comparison table in the paper: Bologna 2021 R2 0.61 / 31 % of roads GEH < 5; Barcelona Virtual Mobility Lab (macroscopic) R2 0.77.published 30 December 2021 (ISPRS Int. J. Geo-Inf. 11(1) 24, CC BY); open copy in the ETH Research Collection (doi 10.3929/ethz-b-000529728); no later release readIt publishes the NEGATIVE result - that a large-scale traffic twin with cell-phone data and surveys still struggles to capture real dynamics - and, now read in full, it is this library's one complete case of a city-scale twin that ran a GENERIC ACTUATED controller at every one of 2,035 core signals because the city's plans were unavailable, on the FULL 2.06 M-trip demand rather than a sample, at ~30 h a run, and still reported R2 0.81 against 488 count stations. It names assignment (iSAR vs IIDUE) and through traffic as what moved the fit; signals were held fixed at 'actuated' throughout.

Tallinn (Estonia) - SimMobility MT Preday activity-based model, with a dynamic-assignment equilibrium loopSimMobility MT 'Preday' (MIT/SMART lineage) for the activity-based demand, coupled to a dynamic traffic assignment for supply; Aalto University / Tallinn University of Technology (Agriesti, Kuzmanovski, Hollmen, Roncoli, Nahmias-Biran)Tallinn, Estonia - 'a population of ~400.000 synthetic individuals, matching the city's whole population'; 'more than 1,100,000 trips in a typical day'. FULL population, not a sample.survey shares + trip totals + OD matrix. Calibrated and reported against THREE simultaneous target families: OD matrix match, mode-share distribution, and employment coverage. The equilibrium paper adds morning car-trip totals (~103,000-113,000 legs, 7.9% error) and work/education trip distributions. NO per-mode transit ridership counts, so it does not reach the top rung.'The error for the overall number of trips is equal to 4% and the average error in the OD matrix is 15.92 vehicles per day.' Mode-share predictions matched observed data across four modes (figures not read). The equilibrium loop reaches 'values of the measure of error lower than 10%' in 15 iterations - final 12% (morning) and 8% (afternoon).active - Bayesian-optimisation paper arXiv 2302.03480 (Feb 2023), published in IEEE Open Journal of Intelligent Transportation Systems; equilibrium-seeking paper arXiv 2404.07789 (2024)The LARGEST published simultaneous parameter calibration of an activity-based model, and the only one read in seven passes that states its own cost honestly. It calibrates 477 behavioural parameters across nested-logit utility functions - 'prior literature had only tackled up to 98 parameters' - against a custom objective combining THREE EQUALLY WEIGHTED components (OD matrix, mode-share distribution, employment coverage), using Bayesian optimisation over an improved Random Forest surrogate. It ran up to 500 iterations, reaching satisfactory performance at iteration 150-182, with each individual run taking '6-8 hours on a laptop' for the full population. It also publishes a SEPARATE architecture for the demand/supply equilibrium: an equilibrium-seeking search that measures 'the difference in traffic patterns between consecutive iterations' and needs 15 iterations to bring it under 10%.

    calibration_tooling
    Three named routes, all read this pass: (1) matsim.calibration in matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools - an ASCCalibrator driving an Optuna study, whose update is literally log(z_i) - log(m_i) - (log(z_0) - log(m_0)), i.e. the classic ASC fixed-point loop normalised on a fixed reference mode, with a pluggable learning-rate scheduler and a TerminationCondition dataclass whose check_termination carries "# TODO: not used yet"; (2) Cadyts, a Bayesian count calibration that adjusts NO parameter and instead adds a utility bonus so agents select the plans matching observed counts; (3) opdyts (Flotterod, TR-B 2017), which approximates point equilibria of the mobsim/scoring/replanning loop, with a Berlin mode-constant example. See calibration_methods. | 2026-09-14: the METHOD NOTE behind route (1) is now read in full - Rakow & Nagel, 'Automated calibration of alternative specific constants in agent based transport models', TU Berlin, June 2024, doi 10.14279/depositonce-20593, CC BY 4.0, three pages. Verbatim: 'Perform a simulation run until convergence and collect all relevant trips. Let z_i be the reference mode share for mode i and m_i the simulated mode share. One ASC always has to be fixed (usually to 0); otherwise, the solution is not unique ... asc_i + ln z_i - ln m_i - (ln z_0 - ln m_0) ... Perform more simulation runs while updating asc_i by delta_i for all modes i, except i = 0 after each run. This is done until simulated mode shares are sufficiently close to the reference mode shares.' Proof given for two alternatives under fixed utilities; discussion: 'The proof assumes that utilities remain constant during simulation runs, which is often not the case ... it is recommended to adjust the update step delta_i by a fraction. This fraction can be modified based on the difference between simulated and reference mode shares.' No run count, no scenario, no fit figure, no distance term in the note; the tooling's ASCDistCalibrator adds distance-group constants with the same update. The idea is credited to Gunnar Floetteroed. This is the exact expression in this project's asc_fixed_point.py, and it is cited as the calibration tool by the Rotterdam-The Hague row (Li et al. 2025).

    restart_mechanism
    NO checkpoint/resume exists in the platform. The developer answer (Marcel Rieser, matsim-code-examples issue #834, 12 Dec 2022, read via api.github.com this pass): 'The plans in "it200/200.plans.xml.gz" are the plans after replanning, but before mobsim, in iteration 200. So you can use those to resume at iteration 200 (it should generate the same events file like the first run), and then continue with iteration 201.' and 'If you use the plans file of iteration 200, start the new run also with iteration 200.' ... 'The first iteration of a run never does replanning.' So a resume is a plans-file restart AT the checkpoint iteration, and only where a plans dump exists (writePlansInterval); everything since the last dump is lost. Memory rule of thumb from the same repository's issue #189: 'typically... around 100KB per agent. That is 1 GB per 10k agents' (mrieser, 2019-08-20); a ~1M-agent, 250k-link scenario needed 60-90 GB actual (mrieser); JVM total is ~25% above the reported heap (josiekre).

A1AResidential location (fixed from census)INB.population.home_jitter_radius_factor = 0.6 (assumed, sweep 0.3-1.0); src/build/build_population.py:46 and :472 (jitter radius from zone area), :463-467 (households drawn per SA1 from census G34 vehicles and G36 dwelling marginals)noneResidential self-selection is a measured but minority share of the built-environment effect: disentangling it by housing type in one study put self-selection at 15.2%, 30.7%, 18.5% and 5.9% of the total impact on vehicle kilometres travelled for the four housing types examined, and the effect is modest for the elderly and large for younger adults. The built-environment side remains the Ewing-Cervero meta-analysis, with every 5D elasticity inelastic. A residence fixed from the census therefore carries most of the built-environment effect and mis-states only the self-selected minority.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S02642751210018522026-09-07
A2AWorkplace locationINsrc/build/build_zone_attractions.py:100-128 (attr_HW = place-of-work jobs disaggregated WPP SA2 -> SA1 by D.attraction.job_weight_by_category, assumed); src/build/build_activity_chains.py:118 (PURPOSES incl. HW), :526-560 balance_destinations under B.activity.destination_balancing = doubly_constrained (definition); B.external.commute_share_to_core = 0.1377 (measured, 2011 census JTW)noneWorkplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice and validate residence-to-work flows against the census commuting table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution. What the field does NOT publish is a flow TOLERANCE. The FHWA validation manual chapter 3 states there are no criteria guidelines for trip-distribution checks, and AToM - the leading open Australian activity- and agent-based model, and the source of several of this project's own behavioural coefficients - validates work travel only as a MODE SHARE of work trips, against a stated plus-or-minus one per cent error threshold on the 2016 Census Method of Travel to Work: driving 74.8% simulated against 73.4% VISTA and 75.2% census; public transport 21.5 / 21.4 / 19.3; walking 2.1 / 2.5 / 3.7; cycling 1.6 / 2.7 / 1.7. Destination distributions are shown only VISUALLY, at SA3 level, with no quantitative flow metric reported, and non-work trips are far looser (walking 15.4% simulated against 23.1% in VISTA). The transferable benchmark for a workplace-location build is therefore: work-trip mode share inside about one percentage point of the census table, plus a visual destination check - not an origin-destination pair tolerance, which no Australian activity-based model publishes.https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2112.120712026-09-08
A3AVehicle ownership per householdINsrc/build/build_population.py:463-465 (household_vehicles from census G34 marginal); B.population.vehicle_roster = census (assumed, categorical census|per_person); src/java/citysim/HouseholdVehicleRoster.java:1-25 (a household drives the cars the census says it owns); src/java/citysim/HouseholdCarDepartureHandler.java:82-110 (a driver whose household car is out waits at the link); RUN.qsim.vehicle_behavior = teleport (assumed); RUN.mode_choice.consider_car_availability = true (definition)noneHousehold car ownership is one of the strongest single predictors of mode: an increase in car ownership raises the probability of commuting by car and depresses active and transit modes, with a reported elasticity of -2.643 for the substitution of active modes. Income, household size, distance to centre, accessibility to shops/services/employment and intersection density are the dominant explanatory variables.https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S13619209240004402026-09-07
A4AVehicle type (EV, e-bike)OUTgrep of cities/newcastle/registry/*.json, src/build/*.py, src/java/citysim/*.java and cities/newcastle/build/*.py for ev_|electric|e-bike|ebike|e_bike finds no field, no attribute and no mechanism; RUN.qsim.car_vehicle = {length 7.5, width 1.0, pce 1.0} (definition) is the single car type; C.scoring.motorbike_fuel_ratio and C.scoring.monetary_distance_rate are fleet averagesnoneThe e-bike evidence is now meta-analysed: across experimental studies, access to an e-bike adds about 5 km of daily travel and raises e-bike mode share by about 26 percentage points, while car use falls by about 2.4 km a day (a 10% drop in car mode share); single controlled trials report car share falling 21%, and older meta-studies put e-bike-for-car substitution at 43% of trips and 63% of mileage. The effect is context-dependent: where cycling is already high the e-bike substitutes conventional cycling; where it is low it draws from car and public transport. (Figures are abstract-level; the full text was not retrievable this pass.)https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/01441647.2025.24745562026-09-07
A5ALicence holdingINB.population.licence_rate_by_age_band (measured, proportional sweep 0.05) and the per-LGA table data/processed/observed/licence_rates_by_age_lga.csv read at src/build/build_population.py:100-134 (licence_rate(sa1, b)), drawn at :349; B.population.licence_min_age = 16 (definition); src/build/build_matsim_plans.py:447-458 (licence holders per household -> car_available); RUN.mode_choice.consider_car_availability = true (definition); B.activity.escort_requires_licence = true (derived)noneLicence holding among people under 35 has fallen across Australia, the UK, the US, Canada and much of Europe: TfNSW reports 65.4% of 16-20 year olds licensed in 2017, 8.3 points below 2001 and 8.1 below 2009, with the proportion licensed at age 30 also declining cohort on cohort. The travel-behaviour consequence named is a greater reliance on getting a lift, especially in wealthy suburbs and high-car-ownership families, and more public transport, walking and cycling in less wealthy areas.https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/system/files/media/documents/2017/Why%20are%20young%20people%20driving%20less%20-%20Trends%20in%20licence-holding%20and%20travel%20behaviour_0.pdf2026-09-07
A6APublic-transport passes / concessionsPARTIALsrc/java/citysim/PtFareChargeHandler.java:272-304 (RiderClass FREE/CHILD/SENIOR/ADULT from the age attribute and employment != employed_full_time), :336-342 daily caps, :445-452 senior per-fare cap; A.fare.child_min_age = 4, A.fare.child_max_age = 15, A.fare.senior_per_fare_cap = 2.5, A.fare.daily_cap_adult/child/senior and *_weekend (observed); A.fare.senior_min_age = 60 (literature, sweep 60-67); A_supply.json:3147 'eligible school students 16+ also qualify; that concession class is recorded, not modelled'noneA smartcard natural experiment on Dutch fares separates pass holders from single-ticket users: passengers on a monthly or annual subscription have the highest travel frequency per origin-destination pair per week - almost twice that of single-ticket users - and the estimated fare elasticities split cleanly between the frequent-user products (pay-as-you-go, student and subscription) and the occasional ones (end-of-month and single tickets). E6ECar availability and competition for household carsINRUN.mode_choice.chain_based_modes (definition, [car, bike]) and RUN.mode_choice.consider_car_availability (definition, true); carAvail written per person from the census car_available at src/build/build_matsim_plans.py:1418; licence from B.population.licence_rate_by_age_band (measured); rideAvail derived as 'household holds a vehicle AND contains another licence holder' (src/java/citysim/AvailabilityModesCalculator.java:25-29); B.population.vehicle_roster = census (assumed, categorical census|per_person) -> HouseholdVehicleRoster installed at src/java/citysim/CitysimControler.java:437 and HouseholdCarDepartureHandler at :494-496, 'A driver whose household car is out waits for it' (src/java/citysim/HouseholdCarDepartureHandler.java:22, :102-108); C.constraint.passenger_per_driver (derived, 0.3503) is DECLARED AHEAD OF ITS CONSUMER (check_hardcoding ledger, issue #31).car +8.5 % (the availability definition decides the car constant)Car availability is the binding constraint on mode, not a preference: the elasticity of active-mode use with respect to car ownership is about -2.6, and the resource logic is that a chain-based mode can only be used if the vehicle is where the traveller left it. E7EPerson attributes: age and sexPARTIALAge gates: B.population.bike_min_age (assumed, 12, sweep 0-16) -> modeAvailability.bikeMinAge and B.taxi.min_unaccompanied_age (assumed, 18, sweep 0-18) -> modeAvailability.taxiMinAge (src/java/citysim/ModeAvailabilityConfigGroup.java:28-31; src/java/citysim/AvailabilityModesCalculator.java:89-109, :245-250); licence by age band B.population.licence_rate_by_age_band (measured) and rider licence B.population.rider_licence_rate_by_age_band (derived); fare class by age at src/java/citysim/PtFareChargeHandler.java:291-297; sex is used only to draw labour-force status in src/build/build_population.py:174-218 - grep sex|female|gender over src/java/citysim and src/build/build_matsim_plans.py returns nothing.noneAge and sex segment travel with a transferable magnitude on the ACTIVE modes. Across 19 major cities in 13 countries and 6 continents (8 low-and-middle-income, 11 high-income), females are more likely than males to walk in every city - on average 23% more likely - and on average 6% more likely to use public transport, while the relation REVERSES for cycling, where women are typically about half as likely to cycle as men; in high-cycling cities the two genders are equally likely, and in Berlin, Munich and Hamburg women cycle more than men. The gap is age-dependent: among children under 16 the metrics are often equal, and the disparity widens with age. On age itself, older travellers drive, walk and take taxis and make little use of bicycles or rideshare, car use falls and dependence on transit rises as the ability to drive falls, and older women are the group most likely to use public transport; an urban Italian study puts men at ~1.5x the odds of choosing a private car over an active mode. No Australian mode-choice model published an age or sex coefficient this pass could read.https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7614415/2026-09-07

E9EBuilt form: density, diversity, design, distance to transitPARTIALBuilt form reaches the run physically: the footpath network A.network.path_modes_by_class (definition; 40,203 footway/path/cycleway ways joined to the roads at 26,615 shared nodes, src/build/build_matsim_network.py:98-103), destination attraction D.attraction.purpose_weight and D.attraction.job_weight_by_category (assumed, sweep +/-40 %, src/build/build_zone_attractions.py), parking search time scaled by the zone's job-density weight (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1171-1186); no registry field or scoring term for density, diversity, intersection density or distance to transit (grep density|diversity|intersection over C_behaviour.json: none); distance to transit enters only as the routed access walk (E28).noneEwing and Cervero's meta-analysis of the built-environment literature to 2009 is the benchmark: VMT per capita is most strongly related to destination accessibility and secondarily to street-network design; walking relates most strongly to land-use diversity, intersection density and destination counts within walking distance; bus and train use relate equally to proximity to transit and network design, with diversity secondary. F1FRoute choice and re-routingINRUN.replanning.weights = {ChangeExpBeta 0.7, ReRoute 0.15, SubtourModeChoice 0.1, TimeAllocationMutator 0.05} (literature) bound to replanning.strategysettings[*].weight; RUN.travel_time.bin_size_s = 300 (literature) / analysed_modes = [car] / separate_modes = false / aggregator = optimistic (assumed) bound to travelTimeCalculator.*; RUN.scoring.path_size_logit_beta = 1.0 (literature) bound to scoring.pathSizeLogitBeta but its own description says 'inert under the shipped RUN.replanning.plan_selector_for_removal = WorstPlanSelector'; A.bike_stress.representation = felt_time (assumed) -> BikeStressDisutility; A.gradient.representation = link_speed -> GradientLinkSpeed; config/schema/matsim_defaults.json:172 pathSizeLogitBeta 1.0.noneRoute choice is estimated on GPS-observed routes with path-size logit corrections for overlapping paths, and the observed share taking the shortest path is small: over 25,157 trips by 143 subjects tracked for 8-13 weeks in Minneapolis-St Paul, 34% of all trips exactly matched the shortest-travel-time path and 40% matched within a 10% tolerance, while for commute trips alone the figures were 13.5% and 21.7%; no subject followed a shortest-DISTANCE path unless it coincided with the shortest-time one. About 50% of trips were within 30 s and about 90% within 5 minutes of the shortest-time route, so the deviation is wide in route space and narrow in time. The plan set is the agent's choice set, and MATSim's recommended control is fractionOfIterationsToDisableInnovation rather than a per-strategy disable iteration. ADDED 8 September 2026: what the loop is converging TO is stated by MATSim's own equilibrium work - an approximate minimisation of an equilibrium gap that measures, per agent, how much it could improve by changing its plan while all others keep theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium'. Reproducible computation of a point equilibrium is named as the single most important advantage of the four-step model that MATSim does not have by default. See the new factor 'Equilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?'.https://matsim.org/docs/userguide/terminology.html2026-09-08
H5HLLM-driven agentsOUTgrep -i 'llm|openai|anthropic|language model' over src/ (py, java) and cities/newcastle/registry/*.json = 0 hits; no registry field, no module.noneTwo 2025-2026 results now bracket this lane. On the optimistic side, GATSim integrates LLM-powered generative agents - hierarchical memory, multi-modal retrieval, planning, reactive and reflection processes, diverse socioeconomic profiles and lifelong learning - into an urban mobility environment, and reports validation at microscopic and macroscopic levels, claiming agents 'perform competitively with human annotators in role-playing scenarios' while 'naturally producing realistic macroscopic traffic patterns'; its abstract states no accuracy figure, no real city and no cost per agent-day. On the sceptical side, the first systematic evaluation against observed mobility (2026) measures AgentSociety and CitySim over Greater Paris (3,337 residents, 7 days) and Shanghai (58,502 users, 10 days) and separates 'face validity' from 'objective mobility realism': AgentSociety's travel-distance error is a Wasserstein distance of 14.83 plus or minus 0.35 km and CitySim's 7.53 plus or minus 1.67 km, with origin-destination similarity at a common-part-of-commuters of 0.138 plus or minus 0.018; trip-duration error is 24.41 plus or minus 0.24 minutes and dwell-time error 3.96 plus or minus 0.12 hours, against reference-sample variability of 0.29 minutes and 0.26 hours. Activity PROPORTIONS come out well (Jensen-Shannon divergence 0.0296) while activity SEQUENCES do not (0.1125), and mobility diversity is 'unstable across default prompting configurations'. The finding to carry: LLM agents reproduce qualitative mobility laws and aggregate activity mixes, and miss individual spatial behaviour by one to two orders of magnitude more than sampling error.https://arxiv.org/html/2606.138352026-09-08
H6HEquilibrium: is the replanning loop a fixed point, and does it converge?PARTIALRUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp = 0.5 (assumed, sweep 0.1-1.0) and RUN.relaxation.settle_margin_iterations = 10 (measured, sweep 1-100) read at src/analyse/summarise_run.py:70-79 and applied in relaxation() at :139-155 (window starts at cutoff + settle margin, verdict 'settled' only inside a stated window); grep -i 'greedo|equilibrium gap|equilibrium_gap|relative_gap' over src/ = 0 hits.noneMATSim's mobsim/scoring/replanning loop is a Monte-Carlo co-evolutionary search, not a solved fixed point, and its own authors say so. Floetteroed's statement of the position is the clearest available: the assignment relies on approximate minimisation of an EQUILIBRIUM GAP measuring, for every agent, how much that agent could improve its score by changing its plan if all other agents kept theirs; 'the gap is always non-negative and zero at a (possibly non-existing) Nash equilibrium', and the method 'aims to reduce the gap in subsequent MATSim iterations, steering the simulation process towards a state that has a low gap, and hence may be deemed to be near an equilibrium point'. He names the reproducible computation of point equilibria as 'the single most important advantage' of the traditional four-step / static-assignment model - an advantage MATSim does not have by default - and supplies the emulation and greedo contribs that add gap minimisation to the loop, illustrated on a multimodal Greater Stockholm scenario with all-day route, departure-time and mode choice. The wider theory agrees: MATSim targets a STOCHASTIC user equilibrium (minimum PERCEIVED cost) rather than a Nash equilibrium; best-response dynamics carry no convergence guarantee, though if they converge they converge to an equilibrium. No published convergence rate exists for a multimodal MATSim scenario: relaxation is asserted by observation, not proved.https://ethz.ch/content/dam/ethz/special-interest/baug/ivt/ivt-dam/events/2023/09/05/abstracts/Floetteroed_MUM_2023.pdf2026-09-08
H7HIn-loop parameter estimation from a ground-truth subpopulationOUTgrep -i 'ground_truth|groundtruth|planParamCalibration|cma_es|cmaes|KeepLastSelected' over src/ = 0 hits; src/calibrate/calibrate.py:4-6 'structurally unable to read a holdout row' and :370 audit_no_holdout(); src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py:2 'One round of the alternative-specific-constant fixed point. PROPOSES ONLY'; src/calibrate/solve_asc_ride.py:4-17 the ride constant is solved from a constraint, not estimated.noneAn architecture that avoids the outer loop entirely: estimate the utility parameters INSIDE the simulation, against a subpopulation of real survey respondents whose observed plans are pinned. The MATSim planParamCalibration extension does exactly that - a designated subpopulation carries its surveyed plan under the KeepLastSelected strategy so those plans are the ground truth, the remaining agents generate alternatives by the ordinary strategies, and CMA-ES maximises a logit-like log-likelihood over the planCalcScore parameters (mode constants, marginal utility of travelling, of distance and of money, daily monetary constants, typical and minimal activity durations, line-switch, waiting, late-arrival and early-departure terms) at each MATSim iteration, writing the result back into the config for the next one. It stops on a designated iteration or on convergence, the default being an average estimated difference below 0.001. Tested on a 2023 street-interview trip-diary survey plus mobile-location commuting arrays at 100 m grid accuracy, the maximum log-likelihood is stable over twenty MATSim iterations and essentially unchanged whether the calibration population is respondents alone or respondents plus 100k, 300k, 600k or one million commuting records - the claimed proof that the estimator is auto-adaptive to population scale. The price of the architecture is exactly the data an aggregate-only city lacks: the likelihood's observations are unit-record plans.https://www.matsim.org/conferences/mum2024/presentations/MUM2024_Lu.pdf2026-09-08
H8HMachine-learned choice models in place of a hand-specified utilityOUTgrep 'sklearn|xgboost|torch|tensorflow|lightgbm' over src/ = 0 hits; RUN.scoring.translation = c1_translation (definition) is the only scoring source and src/build/build_params.py:40-41 expands C.vot.by_purpose (literature) into the C1 table.noneNeural choice models beat multinomial logit on prediction and lose on the quantity a twin is actually scored on. A utility-informed neural network trained on 14,671 trips from the 2017 US National Household Travel Survey for California reached 89.03% mode-choice accuracy, the highest in its benchmark against MNL and other classifiers; alternative-specific-utility deep networks (ASU-DNN) and residual-logit hybrids (ResLogit) are likewise consistently more accurate than MNL on the same data. The published caution is sharper than the accuracy claim: the models with the best DISAGGREGATE predictive performance - gradient-boosted trees and random forests - give POORER estimates of behavioural indicators and of AGGREGATE MODE SHARES than deep neural networks and than plain multinomial logit. Every method in this family is estimated on unit-record choice observations with the alternatives' attributes attached; none can be fitted to a published aggregate share table, and none has been shown to sit inside an equilibrium loop where the attributes of the alternatives are themselves simulation outputs.https://arxiv.org/html/1909.074812026-09-08

The profession's own validation guidance is explicit that this is 'a last resort' after other checks are exhausted - 'the constants can easily be revised so that modeled mode shares match targets', which is precisely the danger, since a constant absorbs every omitted variable and every supply error along with the genuine preference. In an agent-based model the problem is harder than in a four-step model because the attributes of the alternatives are outcomes of the simulation, so the constants cannot be estimated by ordinary maximum likelihood at all; the MATSim-native answer (Rakow and Nagel 2024) is a simulation-based calibration that fine-tunes the ASCs to align simulated mode shares with reference data, and eqasim does the same through boptx.https://tfresource.org/topics/Model_Validation_and_Reasonableness_Checking_Mode_Choice.html2026-09-08
I7IAutomatic calibration: the search algorithm and its evaluation budgetPARTIALsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py:527-575 plan_search 'coordinate descent' with evals = sum(grid points)*max_rounds (:565), :618-686 run_search_and_record, :417 grid(); CAL.search.points_per_parameter = 3 (assumed, sweep [3,7]); CAL.search.max_rounds = 3 (assumed, sweep [1,6]); CAL.search.convergence_delta = 24.88 (derived = CAL.search.reading_drift_pct, measured, sweep [15.72,24.88]); CAL.objective.independent_targets = 10 (derived) caps free parameters (:699); cities/newcastle/params/C5_calibration.json best_tag '20260909T015217_300it_25pct', free_parameters [], history [] - 'CONSTRAINED, not fitted'noneCalibrating a microsimulation is a black-box, stochastic, expensive simulation-based optimisation problem, and the published methods separate by how many simulation evaluations they can afford. SPSA (simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation) is the field's workhorse because it costs only two simulation evaluations per gradient estimate whatever the dimension, and W-SPSA extends it with a weight matrix; but it is built for asymptotic guarantees rather than early termination, and under a small budget it barely moves - on a Salt Lake City origin-destination calibration of order thirty thousand dimensions SPSA took the vehicle-count nRMSE from 120% to 117% over fifteen simulation iterations, while a metamodel method reached 32%. Evolutionary strategies (CMA-ES, xNES) and finite-difference gradient approximation (FDSA, SPSA) are what the MATSim/eqasim calibration framework boptx implements. The cross-entropy method is a Monte-Carlo importance-sampling search and is the most expensive family: one published SUMO calibration of a three-intersection model spent 98,304 simulation evaluations. Bayesian optimisation over a surrogate is the current answer for a small budget (see the surrogate row). The field states its own constraint plainly: computational budgets in the literature are 'one to two orders of magnitude lower than the problem dimension', and general-purpose algorithms 'are designed for asymptotic performance guarantees and are not designed to be terminated with such few function evaluations'.https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.113922026-09-08
I8ISurrogate / metamodel-assisted calibrationOUTgrep -i 'surrogate|metamodel|gaussian|kriging|random_forest|bayesian' over src/calibrate, src/analyse, src/run: 0 hits; docs/positions/runs-and-economics.md:49 'A surrogate/emulator calibration route is held in reserve'noneThe canonical line is Osorio's metamodel simulation-based optimisation: replace the expensive simulated objective with an analytical network model plus a low-order statistical correction, then solve a sequence of cheap analytical problems, so that good points are found from the first iterations without a large initial sample. Its strongest published demonstration is a Salt Lake City origin-destination calibration of order thirty thousand dimensions, where within ONE simulation iteration the linear-metamodel method took the vehicle-count nRMSE from 120% to 32%, against 48% for a tailored linear-assignment method and 117% for SPSA, all inside a fifteen-simulation-iteration budget - and 'thereafter there is not much improvement within such few iterations', i.e. nearly all the gain arrives at the first evaluation. The second family is machine-learned rather than analytical: a random-forest surrogate driving Bayesian optimisation calibrated 477 behavioural parameters of the SimMobility MT activity-based model for Tallinn, and did so against AGGREGATE benchmarks ('the modal share of the whole population'), reaching 4% error on the total number of trips and an average origin-destination error of 15.92 vehicles per day. That paper states no prior work had calibrated as many as 477 parameters and that existing rigorous methods 'do not consider more than a few dozen of parameters (the maximum number being 98)'.https://arxiv.org/pdf/2302.034802026-09-08
I9IIdentifiability under many simultaneous targetsPARTIALCAL.objective.independent_targets = 10 (derived) 'the loop refuses to move more free parameters than this'; src/calibrate/calibrate.py:31-37 'It refuses to fit more parameters than the data identifies', :699 n_free_allowed; src/calibrate/fit.py:22-25 '13 of the 67 identify nothing in MATSim... roughly four mode-share degrees of freedom'; fit.py:499-502 lr_scheduled_runtime marked unscorable 'a schedule INPUT'; grep 'eligib' in src/calibrate: 0 hitsnoneA parameter set is identified only if distinct parameter values produce distinguishable outputs on the targets you actually hold, and the simulation-calibration literature is explicit that when a model is over-parametrised relative to its targets, 'non-identifiability can arise, making it theoretically impossible to locate the true parameter value'. The published remedy is not a better optimiser but a different answer: report an ELIGIBILITY SET - the set of all parameter values whose simulated outputs match the data - constructed to carry rigorous frequentist guarantees, extended to multivariate outputs by a feature-extraction-then-aggregation construction. The counting rule underneath is what binds a mode-share calibration: K shares that sum to one contain K-1 independent numbers, so scoring twelve modelled modes against a five-mode survey does not supply twelve independent targets. The only way to buy identifiability for more parameters is to add targets of a DIFFERENT kind - link counts, boardings, trip-length and duration distributions - not more shares of the same total. The OD-calibration literature reaches the same place from the other side: 'the problem is underdetermined ... there are typically an infinite number of vectors x that can reproduce these counts', which is why a regularisation term toward a prior seed matrix is standard.https://arxiv.org/pdf/2105.128932026-09-08
I10IEstimating choice parameters from aggregate data onlyPARTIALsrc/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py:17-25 aggregate share inversion ('the same object as the Berry (1994) inversion of shares onto constants'), :28-33 boardings-basis rows marked basis_is_boardings proxy; src/calibrate/solve_asc_ride.py:27 constrained solve of C.asc.car_passenger against C.constraint.passenger_per_driver = 0.3503 (derived from C.constraint.vehicle_occupancy = 1.3503, measured, sweep [1.2493,1.394]); cities/newcastle/extract/extract_hts.py:1-9 reads aggregate LGA/SA3 workbooks only; C5_calibration.json history []noneThree distinct families exist for a city with no unit-record survey. (1) AGGREGATE ASC ADJUSTMENT, the practice standard: iteratively add the log ratio of observed to modelled share to each mode constant, re-run, repeat until the split is inside a stated threshold, commonly plus or minus one percentage point; ActivitySim adjusts tour-level and trip-level constants together with the same increment because tour mode conditions trip mode. The profession's own validation manual warns that revising constants is 'a last resort' after other checks are exhausted, because a constant absorbs every omitted variable. (2) BLP-STYLE DEMAND INVERSION: a contraction mapping inverts observed market shares to implied mean utilities and GMM on instrumented moments recovers heterogeneous taste coefficients 'from only aggregate market-share data', removing the IIA restriction on substitution; the requirement is instruments with genuine cross-market variation, which a single-city model does not naturally possess. (3) SURROGATE-ASSISTED SIMULATION-BASED ESTIMATION against aggregate benchmarks: the Tallinn SimMobility work fitted 477 behavioural parameters entirely against 'aggregate benchmarks (e.g., the modal share of the whole population)' and names disaggregate data only as future work - a direct feasibility proof that unit records are not a precondition for fitting a large behavioural parameter set.https://tfresource.org/topics/Model_Validation_and_Reasonableness_Checking_Mode_Choice.html2026-10-07

I11ISequential versus simultaneous calibration of many targetsPARTIALsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py:20-23 objective is ONE scalar (max over twelve modes) evaluated simultaneously, :566-567 parameters moved sequentially by coordinate descent, :54-57 'Constraints are constraints, not targets' (occupancy and trip length never enter the objective, infeasible candidates marked), :46-52 counts excluded (CAL.objective.include_counts = false, derived); C5_calibration.json history [] (never executed)noneThe field states the choice explicitly and it is a real fork, not a matter of taste. In dynamic OD calibration, 'the first formulation estimates the whole set of time-dependent OD matrices SIMULTANEOUSLY for the entire time period in one calibration round. The second formulation estimates and calibrates OD matrices SEQUENTIALLY one at a time for each time frame. Most optimization-based studies have used the simultaneous approach, since the available sequential methods may lose accuracy due to giving up some information in the transition between time frames' - while the simultaneous form 'is incapable of handling a stream of data for real-time or online demand calibration'. The same paper states the bind that makes the choice matter at all: 'this optimization problem is underdetermined for large-scale networks since the number of roads with traffic measurement is usually several orders of magnitude smaller than the number of all roads in the network', and it names the standard architecture as BI-LEVEL - an upper-level discrepancy minimisation over an inner assignment that must be re-solved at every candidate, where 'performing several DTAs for each optimization task demand considerable computational resources'. In DTA practice the sequential form is supply first and then demand with the supply held fixed; the reported weakness of decomposing is that the stages need not be internally consistent, because each stage's assumed input is not the other stage's output.https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.173152026-09-09
I12IDamping and step-size schedule in the constant-adjustment contractionPARTIALCAL.asc.damping = 0.6 (literature, sweep [0.3,1.0]) 'How much of the raw log-ratio step an ASC round applies'; CAL.asc.max_step_utils = 1.5 (definition, held_fixed) refuses a larger step; src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py:111 damping = cfg.get('CAL.asc.damping'), :173-174 raw = ln(1/ratio) - ref_term; step = damping*raw, :198-204 refusal past max_step, :226 contraction(); no schedule (no linear_scheduler equivalent); no round output on disknoneThe log-ratio ASC step is a contraction only if it is damped, and the two open implementations of it disagree on how. The leading open MATSim calibrator, matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools, computes the raw step verbatim as 'math.log(z_i) - math.log(m_i) - (math.log(z_0) - math.log(m_0))' and applies it under a SCHEDULE whose default is 'linear_scheduler(start=0.6, end=1, interval=3)' - the early rounds take 0.6 of the raw step and the fraction relaxes to the full step over three intervals, i.e. cautious while the shares are far from target and undamped once they are near. The agency practice in the ActivitySim world applies a FLAT dampener instead of a schedule. Neither publishes a convergence proof, and the same library's 'TerminationCondition.check_termination' still carries '# TODO: not used yet' - so the field's standard answer ships a damping default and no working stopping rule at all. The undamped step (1.0) is the boundary case: it is what a fixed point converges to when it converges, and what overshoots when the shares are far out.https://github.com/matsim-vsp/matsim-python-tools/blob/master/matsim/calibration/utils.py2026-09-09

Jakob and Blume set it out: with a weighted sum, 'by varying the weights, any point of a convex Pareto front can be obtained... On the other hand, it is possible that parts of the Pareto front cannot be found in case of a non-convex problem... the part between points A and B of the Pareto front cannot be obtained for any weights. This is a serious drawback.' The counterweight is cost: 'the computational effort to determine all or at least most of the Pareto front increases significantly with the number of conflicting objectives', and the paper's framing is that the real-world question arises 'where either more than four objectives have to be considered, or the same type of task is repeated again and again with only minor modifications'. The selection protocol before the cutoff 'resembles a MNL choice model', P(i|C) = exp(mu S_i)/sum exp(mu S_j) with mu = brainExpBeta, and the chapter notes that BestPlanSelector is the same selector with an infinite mu. So the pre-cutoff share is a logit-dispersed mixture over each agent's remembered plans and the post-cutoff share is the same population collapsed toward its arg-max: switching innovation off changes the estimator, not only the amount of search. Assignment theory says the same thing from the other side - a low dispersion parameter concentrates flow on the perceived-best alternative and the pattern approaches deterministic user equilibrium, which is the classic 'unrealistic route concentration' that stochastic user equilibrium was introduced to cure. The efficiency loss of that concentration is bounded and modest on real networks - a data-driven estimate for Eastern Massachusetts puts the price of anarchy near 1.30, and other empirical work finds it close to 1 in both light and heavy traffic - so an equilibrium being reached is no guarantee that it resembles the observed day, which is itself a non-equilibrium average.https://matsim.org/docs/userguide/terminology.html2026-09-10

K4KFlow-capacity, storage-capacity and stuck-time correction at a sample fractionINRUN.sample.storage_capacity_exponent = 1.0 (derived) 'IT IS 1.0 AND IT IS NOT FREE'; RUN.sample.flow_capacity_factor / storage_capacity_factor (derived, null = computed per run); src/run/run_matsim.py:530-541 refuses a storage factor differing from the flow factor; src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1923-1928 emits both; RUN.qsim.stuck_time_s = 10.0 (assumed, sweep [10,600]) -> qsim.stuckTime (RUN_execution.json:1397 matsim_param); RUN.qsim.remove_stuck_vehicles = false (assumed, categorical sweep) -> qsim.removeStuckVehicles (:1414); RUN.qsim.link_dynamics = 'PassingQ' (definition); RUN.qsim.traffic_dynamics = 'queue' (assumed, categorical [queue, kinematicWaves]); RUN.sample.transit_pce_scaling = true (derived); check_hardcoding: 164 of 164 bound fields proven to reach the confignoneThe correction rules for a downscaled run are contested and were measured again this year. Mersini and Ziemke (MUM 2025, TU Berlin) set out the position: former recommendations scaled storage less than flow, flowCapacityFactor = sample share and storageCapacityFactor = sample share^alpha with alpha = 0.75 'to prevent breakdowns in small samples', while 'more recently, flow and storage capacities are usually scaled equally, i.e., with alpha = 1', the Open Berlin practice; Llorca and Moeckel found 'no substantial differences in average travel times for a given MATSim scenario when comparing different sample shares using both alpha values', and Ben-Dor, Ben-Elia and Benenson again recommend 0.75. Their measured result on a 100 per cent Lausitz benchmark is that scores and travel times are close to the full-scale run at 25 and 50 per cent, deviate at 5 per cent and clearly at 1 per cent, and that 'even average statistics (such as score and travel time) become unreliable when sampling below 10%'. The sharper finding is on the third parameter nobody scales: stuck-time violations, normalised by the inverse sample share, rise from about 40,000 at 100 per cent (about one agent in eight stuck once per day) to three times as many at 1 per cent, and with equal scaling of flow and storage 'even more than four and a half times as many' - so alpha = 1 costs stuck agents at small samples, and the paper flags that stuck time itself should be scaled with the sample size, larger for smaller samples.https://matsim.org/conferences/mum2025/abstracts/MUM25_paper_30.pdf2026-09-10
