The expansion is only the first of three basis decisions, and the other two are where practice models put their error bars: WHICH simulated vehicles count (the observed detector counts every vehicle class, so the modelled side must either add its heavy vehicles or the observed side must be converted to a light-vehicle basis - one or the other, never neither), and WHICH link a station maps to (a two-way station is the sum of both directions and a station matched to a service road or the wrong carriageway reads near zero). The European review by de Jong and Gunn (2001), as tabulated by Litman, gives car-kilometres with respect to fuel price -0.16 short term and -0.26 long term (commuting -0.12 / -0.23), and car-kilometres with respect to travel time -0.20 short term and -0.74 long term; Goodwin (1996) gives urban-road vehicle travel with respect to travel time -0.27 short run and -0.57 long run. Litman's synthesis states the scaling explicitly: a -0.1 short-run elasticity of vehicle travel with respect to fuel price reflects a -0.3 long-run elasticity, which reflects about -1.2 with respect to total vehicle costs, because most vehicle costs (depreciation, financing, insurance, registration, residential parking) are fixed and short-run effects are about a third of long-run ones. Brons, Nijkamp, Pels and Rietveld's meta-analysis of gasoline-demand price elasticities (158 estimates) finds the demand response driven mainly by fuel efficiency and car ownership and to a lesser degree by mileage per car, with a long-run estimate about -0.46 for total fuel demand. H12HHabit, inertia and satisficing: does the agent re-optimise every day, or stick until a threshold is crossed?ASCgrep -i 'inertia|habit' over src/ (py, java) and cities/newcastle/registry/*.json = 1 hit, prose in src/run/issue_gate.py:56; no registry field and no scoring term; persistence exists only implicitly through RUN.replanning.weights ChangeExpBeta = 0.7 (literature) with RUN.scoring.brain_exp_beta = 1.0 (literature) and RUN.replanning.max_agent_plan_memory = 8; whatever habit does to the observed split lands in the mode constants C.asc.* (assumed/placeholder: bus -1.05, light_rail -0.75, rail -0.65, walk 0.35, cycle -1.35, car_passenger -0.85, motorbike 0.0, ferry -1.05) through src/calibrate/asc_fixed_point.py:2-23 (the Berry inversion of shares onto constants).car +8.5 % (convergence car-heavier than any gate read)Habit is one of the two strongest predictors of the mode a person uses, and it is a MEASURED effect, not a residual. Three meta-analyses put the pooled correlation between a habit measure and the travel mode used at r+ = 0.50 (Gardner & Abraham 2008), r+ = 0.42 (Lanzini & Khan 2017, 58 primary studies) and r = 0.47 (Hoffmann et al. 2017), against an averaged pooled car-use-intention correlation of r+ = 0.83 in Lanzini & Khan; the review of reviews that collects them (Javaid, Creutzig & Bren d'Amour 2020) notes the differences between the meta-analyses exceed their confidence intervals. In discrete-choice terms inertia is the tendency to stick with the past choice even when another alternative becomes more appealing: Cherchi & Manca (2011, Transportation 38:679-695) test eight specifications on an RP/SP dataset with a mixed logit and find a significant, mode-specific inertia that weakens with learning across the SP experiments; Cantillo, Ortuzar & Williams (2007, Transportation Science) model it as a randomly distributed inertia THRESHOLD with serial correlation. The route-choice literature measures the same thing as an INDIFFERENCE BAND: travellers do not switch unless the saving exceeds a threshold (Mahmassani & Liu 1999), and Zhu & Levinson (2016, Transportation) estimate lognormal bands on 78 GPS subjects around the Minneapolis I-35W bridge replacement, which explains why the new bridge attracted less traffic than its time saving predicted. Satisficing (Simon 1957) is the general form - search stops at a satisfactory alternative - and boundedly rational user equilibrium (Di & Liu 2016 review) is the assignment that follows from it. The magnitudes the field reports are correlations and thresholds, not a utility constant; a simulator represents habit either as a state-dependent term (past mode in the utility), as a switching threshold, or - as MATSim does - as a selection rule over remembered plans.https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1748-9326/aba0322026-10-07
F6FTravel-time reliability and route switching: the reliability ratio and the indifference band in route choiceINERTC.time_weights.beta_reliability = 1.3 (literature, sweep 0.8-1.8); C.time_weights.service_quality_representation = absent (assumed, sweep [absent, headway, headway_and_reliability]) bound to serviceQuality.representation; src/java/citysim/ServiceQualityConfigGroup.java:92-96 REPRESENTATION_ABSENT/HEADWAY/BOTH and isEnabled() at :146; src/java/citysim/CitysimControler.java:614-621 installs ServiceQualityScoring only if serviceQuality.isEnabled(); ServiceQualityScoring.java:70-75 reads VehicleArrivesAtFacilityEvent.getDelay() for the reliability charge.bus -30.7 %, light_rail -74.0 % (reliability unpriced)Reliability enters route choice as a second attribute beside mean time, and the field's summary statistic is the RELIABILITY RATIO - the value of a unit of standard deviation over the value of a unit of mean travel time. Carrion & Levinson (2012, TR-A 46(4):720-741) review and meta-analyse the estimates and attribute their spread to measurement (which dispersion measure, SP versus RP, self-reported versus GPS times). The same authors' Minneapolis before-and-after study of the I-35W bridge (39 subjects with complete data, 78 GPS observations) shows how far the ratio moves with measurement alone: 1.30 (mean/SD) and 1.60 (median/SD) on SELF-REPORTED times against 0.42 and 0.77 on GPS-MEASURED times, and 0.83 / 0.39 on the mean-to-90th-percentile measure - a ratio above 1 with perceived times and below 1 with measured ones. Route SWITCHING is boundedly rational: travellers keep their usual route until the saving exceeds an indifference band (Mahmassani & Liu 1999; Zhu & Levinson 2016 estimate lognormal bands on the same 78-subject GPS panel and use them to explain why the replaced bridge attracted less traffic than its time saving implied). For a simulator this means (a) a reliability term in route cost needs a measured day-to-day time variance per link, which a single-day equilibrium simulation does not produce, and (b) the switching rate of the route-choice strategy is itself a behavioural parameter.https://findingspress.org/article/8330-uncovering-the-influence-of-commuters-perception-on-the-reliability-ratio2026-10-07
B7BImmobility: the share of persons who make no trip on the survey dayPARTIALgrep of cities/newcastle/registry/*.json, src/build/*.py and cities/newcastle/build/*.py for immobil|no_travel|zero_trip|stay_home|p_travel finds no field; src/build/build_activity_chains.py:3413 (per-purpose tour counts are independent Poisson draws, so a person is immobile only when every draw and the mandatory draw are zero), :3326 reports travelling_persons; B.activity.hts_rate_per_person_day = 3.473 (measured) sets the leveltrip rate (the immobile share unobserved)Madre, Axhausen & Brog (Transportation 34, 2007) treat the immobile share - persons not leaving home on the reporting day - as both a central result and a prime quality indicator of a travel diary survey: for a standard one-day, weekday-only diary it should lie in the range 8-12 %, and a higher figure signals soft refusal (respondents claiming not to have left the house) rather than a behavioural fact. Later panel work (Transportation 2022, weekly routines of employees and retirees) shows immobile days cluster by person and weekday, so a one-day rate understates the share of people who are ever immobile and overstates the share of habitually immobile people.https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11116-006-9105-52026-10-07
E27EHeavy rail: station access mode - walk, feeder bus, park-and-ride, kiss-and-ridePARTIALRUN.transit_router.access_egress_basis = network (derived) emits swissRailRaptor.intermodalAccessEgress[*].mode = ['walk'] - 'the one access/egress mode: walk' (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:2224-2231); car and bike are chain-based (RUN.mode_choice.chain_based_modes) with no pt access leg, grep -i park.?and.?ride|kiss|feeder over src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py, src/java/citysim and RUN_execution.json: none beyond the walk intermodal set; a feeder bus to a station occurs only as a pt-to-pt transfer inside the raptor under A.transit.transfer_search_radius_m (assumed, 400) and transfer_detour_factor (literature, 1.25) from src/build/build_gtfs_extras.py; an escort to a station exists only as a serve-passenger tour (HX) in the demand, not as an access mode.heavy_rail +119.3 % (walk is the only access mode)Station access is a mode choice of its own and its split moves with distance and supply. In Sydney, walking is the access mode for about half of home-to-train trips and almost 90 % of home-to-bus trips (Daniels & Mulley 2013, from the HTS); TfNSW's rail-user analysis puts walk access at 48 % and walk EGRESS at 84 %, because the car is not available at the far end. Meng, Taylor & Scrafton (ATRF 2017) observed three Adelaide Gawler-line interchanges in 2010: Mawson Lakes - feeder bus 46 %, park-and-ride 27 %, kiss-and-ride 17 %, walk+bike 10 %; Elizabeth - bus 44 %, walk 37 %, park-and-ride 11 %, kiss-and-ride 7 %; Gawler (one occasional bus) - walk 43 %, park-and-ride 36 %, kiss-and-ride 15 %, bus 3 %. Their stated-preference model finds walking distance, bus access, bus waiting time, car access and car-park availability all significant, with age, income and gender effects. Outer-suburban Sydney stations surveyed by Ku-ring-gai Council read car-driver access at 35 % (17-52 % by station). The rule is that park-and-ride grows with distance from the CBD and with free station parking, and that a walk-only access model under-states the catchment of an outer station by roughly the car-access share.https://australasiantransportresearchforum.org.au/wp-content/uploads/2022/03/ATRF2017_114.pdf2026-10-07

Mode of the public-transport trip is the dominant determinant - supply and stop spacing, not the walker - and the distributions are right-skewed with a tail past 1.5 km. Ewing & Cervero's meta-analysis gives a transit-demand elasticity of -0.29 to distance-to-stop (a 10 % longer walk costs about 3 % of ridership). Planning rules of thumb (400 m bus, 800 m rail; NSW's 90 %-of-households-within-400 m daytime standard) are straight-line and shorter than the observed walks.https://www.jtlu.org/index.php/jtlu/article/view/308/3382026-10-07
I16ITravel-time and speed validation: the acceptance bar for link speeds and route travel timesPARTIALgrep -i 'GEH|inrix|tomtom|observed speed' over src/analyse and src/calibrate: 0 hits; src/calibrate/fit.py:499-502 lr_scheduled_runtime unscorable 'a schedule INPUT... reproduces 12.00 min by construction'; fit.py:542-580 score_trip_geometry reports modelled_mean_time_min vs observed_mean_time_min per mode (C.constraint.trip_time_min.*, measured); fit.py:347-362 counts statistics are mean % error and RMSE (no GEH); validation_targets.csv metrics contain no speed or route travel-time rownoneThe FHWA Traffic Analysis Toolbox Volume III (2004; Wisconsin DOT targets, Table 4) is the profession's acceptance table for a calibrated traffic model: hourly link flows within 15 % for 700-2,700 veh/h (within 100 veh/h below 700, within 400 above 2,700) in more than 85 % of cases; the sum of link flows within 5 %; GEH < 5 on individual links in more than 85 % of cases and GEH < 4 on the sum; ROUTE TRAVEL TIMES within 15 % (or one minute if higher) in more than 85 % of cases; link speeds and bottleneck queuing judged visually. The 2019 revision (TxDOT's summary) replaces the fixed bands with a two-sigma band (95 % of simulated points inside) plus two accuracy criteria applied to every metric used for calibration, and requires at least two metrics. Travel time is therefore a first-class validation target alongside counts, and a model that matches counts but not times is not accepted.https://ops.fhwa.dot.gov/trafficanalysistools/tat_vol3/sect5.htm2026-09-16

Nommon's practice note describes the pipeline: a continuous, region-wide sample against a household survey's ~2 % taken once a decade; expansion by classical synthetic-population techniques with census; home, work and study inferred readily, other purposes and the mode only by fusion with smartcard and classified counts, and refined in calibration. Matet, Come, Furno, Horl, Oukhellou & El Faouzi (Transportation 2024) show OD matrices from phone data improving synthetic travel demand generation (the ANR MOBITIC/PROMENADE work with eqasim). The limits are stable across sources: short trips and walking are under-detected, purpose beyond the anchors is inferred, and a privacy-aggregated zonal product needs the OD-estimation methods developed for counts.https://www.nommon.es/blog/transport-models-and-mobile-phone-data/2026-09-16
E29EWalk: the trip-length distribution and its long tail (how far people actually walk)PARTIALC.scoring.marginal_utility_of_distance_per_m walk 0.0 (derived) - no walk distance term; B.mode.walk_feasible_km (derived, 0.0, sweep 0-6, derived_from C.constraint.trip_length_km.walk) is SHIPPED AT THE CONSUMER'S OFF VALUE (check_hardcoding ledger item 7: 'GatedSubtourModeChoice.beyondReach treats a limit of 0 as no limit'), so SubtourModeChoice offers walk at any distance; the only length cost is time at traveling(C.time_weights.beta_walk_mode 1.04, literature) (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1474-1475); C.constraint.trip_length_km.walk (measured, 0.7 km, sweep 0.7-1.1) and trip_time_min.walk (measured, 12.3) are targets and the base of the 3,223.6 m no-route reach, not scoring inputs; docs/STATUS.md:23 traces walk's error on F39's control to 'short trips driven and car-less trips with no alternative'.walk 3.75 km vs 0.70 (-24.7 % share)Walking trips are short and their distribution decays steeply. From the 2009 US National Household Travel Survey, Yang & Diez-Roux (AJPM 2012) report a mean walking trip of 0.7 miles and a median of 0.5 miles (about 1.1 and 0.8 km), a mean duration of 14.9 min and a median of 10 min; about 65 % of walking trips exceed 0.25 mile and only about 18 % exceed 1 mile. Distance and duration vary substantially by purpose (recreational walks are much longer) and by subgroup (lower-income people walk farther for work), and the distribution is summarised by distance-decay functions rather than a cut-off. A simulator whose walk utility is linear in time with no distance term, and whose other alternatives can fail, places mass in a multi-kilometre tail the surveys do not contain.https://digitalcommons.memphis.edu/facpubs/17034/2026-09-25

In Australia a motorcycle travels on average 1.9 thousand km a year against 11.1 thousand km for a passenger vehicle (ABS SMVU 2020), and most owners ride socially (65 % always, 26 % sometimes; 9 % transport-only, 2024 owner survey). The rider licence is a separate, much rarer licence class than the car licence. A model that makes the motorcycle available to every licensed member of a motorcycle-holding household on every day therefore supplies the option far more often than it is exercised; the gap is a daily-availability or use-frequency question, not a taste constant.https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/industry/tourism-and-transport/survey-motor-vehicle-use-australia/latest-release2026-09-29

The document and process layer

layering

as_designed
Goal (docs/GOAL.md) -> Board (docs/STATUS.md, generated blocks + hand lines) -> Brief (docs/NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md) -> Lane (docs/lane.json rendered into both) -> Position (13 pages) -> City (cities/<city>/docs/) -> Record (docs/DECISIONS.md, entered by index) -> Reports (docs/reports/ + reference/). The layering holds: every living document names its layer in its own intro (STATUS.md:3-8, NEXT_AGENT_BRIEF.md:4, positions/*:3, docs/README.md:11-21, HANDOVER_CONTRACT.md:24-32).
exceptions
  • Six framework contract documents sit loose at docs/ root (boarding_fares.md, hired_fleet.md, mode_vehicles.md, network_access.md, person_modes.md, transit_fleet.md; last touched 2026-09-21/22) beside the simulator's living documents, linked from docs/README.md:53-66 - the layer docs/README.md:1-9 defines for docs/ is 'the simulator and its results', and these describe config/schema/ contracts (carried from reports 14 and 15, unchanged).
  • docs/lane.json carries its own top-level family stamp (lane.json:4 = F38) that no layer owns: the ledger (docs/run_families.json, newest key F39) is the one home of the open family and nothing pins the lane's copy to it (lane.py --check validates entry shape only, src/analyse/lane.py:117-150).
  • docs/reports/reference/README.md holds two homes for 'the last pass': its State table (:47-58, '25 September 2026 ... the fourteenth report') and a per-report section appended at the bottom (:258, the fifteenth report) - the table was not rewritten for pass 15.

In-flight work seen in the tree

The tree at the read carried one uncommitted change: .gitignore gains two lines, praneetdhoolia.github.io/ (the blog's clone, which the blog session placed inside this repository) and *.zip (the proposal deck The City Twice - showcase.zip at the root), and loses its trailing newline. It is the blog session's housekeeping, touches no model, data or document, and this session carries it in its own pull request. Nothing else was uncommitted; no commit was ahead of origin/main; no pull request was open; no arm was running (the machine was idle: no Java process above 2 GB). The three 4-iteration treatment probes of 30 September (20260930T111836, T123858, T140500 _4it_25pct) are on disk with records and are citable for their clocks only.

Since the last report, and the report process itself

reading
The fifteenth report read F38's arm 0 (1 of 12) at 6bc18487 on 29 September; this one reads F39's control (2 of 12) at 1b14e559, one reading and one PR (#259) later - the cadence rule (one report per reading) is kept, and the week between carried no commit, session or run.
findings
12 of the fifteenth's 21 findings are fixed at HEAD with code and tests (ranks 1, 2, 4-10, 19-21); 9 are still open or narrowed (ranks 3, 11-18). This pass holds 69 merged findings: 4 defects, 14 risks, 51 smells - two defects are new in code written since (watch_run.py:121, MANIFEST.csv:598) and two are one-city blind spots (session_gate.py:191, check_manifest.py:255).
ratings
Code cells at 4 or better: 10 of 30 then, 11 of 30 now (run harness and MATSim extensions carry three each). Simulator performance 3/4/2/4/3 -> 3/4/3/4/4 (reliability up on one clean arm and the restart guard; cost observability up on the priced-on-its-own-build rule). History 3/4/3/3 unchanged. Documents 2 -> 3; process, controls and issue hygiene 3 unchanged. Model fit: modes inside 10 % 1 -> 2, mechanisms 3, attribution 1 -> 2.
survey_rows
61 project rows (3 added: Meerut, Tel Aviv Pink Route, eqasim Switzerland; 5 refreshed; 2 moved up a rung: Ile-de-France to road link counts, Greater Jakarta to transit ridership counts), 12 platforms unchanged, gaps 29 -> 32 in the array with 7 open (5 closed this pass). Ladder 7 / 14 / 28 / 12 / 0: the top rung is still ours alone.
factor_statuses
108 rows (2 added: E30 car terminal time, E31 the car-less person's lift). Statuses at HEAD: IN 37 / PARTIAL 54 / INERT 5 / ASC 2 / OUT 10 against 48 / 39 / 3 / 2 / 14 - most of the IN-to-PARTIAL movement is a stricter reading of rows the fifteenth stored no status for (the calibration search and ASC round are coded and have never executed); the model changes that moved a class are F7 (the no-route walk bounded, PARTIAL -> IN) and E18 (motorbike chosen by daily use, PARTIAL -> IN). The headway charge (F8, E12) is INERT: built, rebuilt on the line at its stop, declared with ATAP M1, shipped absent, unrun.
recommendations
Of the fifteenth's 20: taken 2 (SMVU daily use, the one that moved the count), 6 (write_plans 25), 8 (records tell the truth about cost), 12-16 and 18-19 in #259; half taken 1 (host load recorded, nothing refuses on it); open 1 (the headway arm - rebuilt, priced, unrun), 3 (one change at a time, its tenth issuance), 6 (survive sign-out), 17 (the TfNSW request, ninth), 20 (the ASC loop, correctly held). The ledger reads 26 of 84 open before this pass's sync.
the_report_itself
Fifteen reports in 58 days; 201 of 261 recommendations taken (77 %); for the first time a model recommendation raised the goal count at a result. What the series still does not buy is attribution: no pair has been read since F35. This report's own repeats are tagged below: the replication band (11th), the TfNSW request (10th), the headway arm (2nd), the sign-out-proof task (2nd), the package audit before an arm (3rd).

verdict

FOLLOWED, AND FOR THE FIRST TIME A REPORT'S MODEL RECOMMENDATION MOVED THE GOAL COUNT UP AT A RESULT. Report #15's recommendation 2 (motorcycle availability by daily use) was built the same day and F39's control read motorbike -4.1 % from +465.7 %: the count went 1 -> 2 with the predicted mode re-entering the band, and the report's 'guard' (motorbike share at the next result) was the thing that scored it. Across the series 201 of 261 recommendations are taken (77.0 %), the ledger holds 58 of 84 (69.0 %), and what the reports buy is still mostly correctness (the holdout leak, the count map, the reader's schedule, the external tier, the headway charge keyed on route variants - caught by #259's probes before a 30 h arm spent on it). What they do not buy is attribution: F39 bundled four corrections into one arm, so 'motorbike -4.1 %' is the one effect that can be attributed (it is the only change touching motorbike), and the walk and pt readings cannot be. The designed pair (control + headway) is half run after eight days - the first time a family has been built as a pair, and the first time the second half has sat unrun this long. CADENCE: 16 reports in 35 days; the once-per-reading rule is kept (this report follows one reading, 8.8 days after the last); but the project has had no session since 30 Sep, so a report now is a report on a quiet week - its value is in the two things only a report can do here: name what is unrun and what is repeated. AGAINST THIS REPORT: any recommendation below that re-asks the replication band (11th), the TfNSW tables (10th), 'one change at a time' (11th), a second reviewer (5th), the package audit before an arm (3rd), travel-time validation (3rd), surviving sign-out (2nd), or the headway arm itself (2nd: built, priced, unrun) is a repeat and should be a lane decision asked once or dropped.
